problems.title: Rejected alternatives mutate the selected continuation
problems.source_location: Algorithm 1, lines 6–9, PDF p.5; DPOAgent.step, lines 180–381
claim: Candidates should execute from the same pre-step history and continue only the selected branch.
analysis: Start with counter \(0\) and empty trail. Candidate A adds \(1\) and appends selected; B adds \(100\) and appends rejected; C prints the counter. The inspected sequential shared-state calls yield observations \(1,101,101\). If A is chosen, its recorded observation is \(1\), but the environment remains at \(101\) with B’s rejected trail entry. Independent branches give \(1,100,0\) and commit counter \(1\). Reordering to C,B,A makes the selected A observe \(101\), showing context contamination rather than merely a stale display. Redefining a helper in B similarly changes the shared custom-tool namespace. Adding two read-only candidates preserves the defect at the paper’s count \(5\).
result: The release violates common-context comparison and selected-state continuation for admissible stateful actions. Pure independent actions can avoid it. Published evaluation disables this sampling path; training-data prevalence and benchmark effect are unestablished.
assumptions: Ordinary assignment/list mutation is permitted. The verifier deliberately selects A, removing verifier-error uncertainty.
repair: Fork the entire relevant execution environment for each candidate and commit only the selected branch. Deep-copying value state repairs the counter/list witness, but does not automatically isolate tool objects, closures, files or external effects.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local implementation or interpretation defect; damage to the central empirical result has not been established.

problems.title: The public constructor ignores an explicit candidate-count override
problems.source_location: create_agent sampling_size construction; Section 4.5 experimental candidate count
claim: The constructor exposes a formal candidate-count argument but reads the effective value from extra keyword arguments with a default.
analysis: A bound formal argument is removed from the extra-keyword dictionary, so looking it up there uses the default \(5\) even after an explicit different request. The paper itself uses \(5\), so this does not challenge its reported setting.
result: This is a minor API observation; no distinct scientific failure is established.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper correction is required for this cleared concern.
